styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Grand Mosque, Mutrah souq and Omani coffee.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Forts, palaces and old Muscat's walls.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Wadis, mountains and dolphin boat trips.

stays.why: Walk to the corniche, fish market and souq. Good for a first visit and evening strolls.
Central and cheap, with bus links. Handy if you are travelling on a budget.
Beaches, cafés and the Royal Opera House nearby. A calm base between old and new Muscat.
Close to the Grand Mosque and the airport road. Good for early flights and mosque visits.

food: Try Omani dishes: shuwa (slow-cooked meat), harees and majboos rice with fish or chicken.
Mutrah fish market: see the catch, then eat grilled fish at simple nearby restaurants.
Omani halwa and dates with cardamom coffee (kahwa) are the classic snack; buy halwa in Mutrah souq.
Cheap eats: shawarma, biryani and cafeteria meals in Ruwi, roughly OMR 1–3 a plate.
Alcohol is limited to licensed hotel restaurants and bars. Dress modestly and ask before photographing people.
more_time: Swap a city day for Nizwa: the fort and Friday goat market, about 1.5–2 hours by car each way.
Add a wadi day: Wadi Shab or Wadi Bani Khalid for pools and walking; check conditions and take a 4WD if unsure.
Take a boat trip from the Marina to watch dolphins, usually a morning outing; book ahead and check the price on the day.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Grand Mosque, Mutrah and old Muscat at an easy pace; add a night for a wadi or Nizwa day trip.

month_notes: January: mild days around 25°C and cool nights. Great for walking and forts.
February: warm and dry, about 26°C. One of the best months to be outside.
March: warming to 29°C. Still comfortable; mornings are best for sightseeing.
April: hot at 34°C. Do outdoor sights early and rest in the afternoon.
May: very hot, 38°C, no rain. Stay indoors midday and drink plenty of water.
June: peak heat at 39°C with warm nights. Plan air-conditioned sights and evening walks.
July: hot and humid, 38°C. Keep outdoor time to early morning or after sunset.
August: similar heat, 37°C. Beaches are warm but the sun is strong; use shade.
September: still hot at 36°C. Slightly easier evenings; carry water everywhere.
October: cooling to 34°C. Better for outdoor trips later in the month.
November: pleasant at 29°C. Good for wadis, forts and the corniche.
December: mild at 26°C with cool nights. A top month for sightseeing.

climate_guide.summary: Hot desert climate: sunny most of the year, very little rain, and a very hot, humid summer from May to September.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Days around 25–29°C and cooler nights. Ideal for forts, the souq and wadi walks.

items.title: Summer is extreme (May to September)
items.text: Highs of 36–39°C with warm nights. Do outdoor sights at sunrise or after dark.

items.title: Humid near the coast
items.text: Muggy evenings in summer; the sea breeze helps but shade and water matter more.

items.title: Almost no rain
items.text: Only a few rain days a year, mostly December to March. No umbrella needed most trips.

items.title: Dust and haze
items.text: Occasional dusty winds can haze the sky and make mountain or wadi trips less pleasant.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes, a hat and strong sunscreen; a light layer for cool winter nights and indoor AC; modest clothing for mosques.

transit.best: Taxi or the OTaxi app for most trips; rent a car for wadis and mountains.

modes.text: No metro or tram. Don't plan around rail in the city.
Mwasalat buses cover key sights and the airport. Fares about 300 baisa to OMR 1; pay the driver in cash and buy a new ticket for each bus.
Orange-and-white taxis are metered-ish; agree the fare first. OTaxi gives fixed fares. Maxi taxis cost about OMR 0.2–0.4 per hop.
Cheap and flexible. A 4WD helps for wadis and mountains. Check your licence and insurance before booking.
Only pleasant November to March, and sights are spread out. Use taxis for longer hops in summer.
